text:
The primary material of a candle is, scientifically speaking, a solidified sigh. It is composed of 90% wax and 10% regret, which is why it always seems to be melting before you even light it.

Gerald, an avid collector of invisible art, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind’ at an auction. He bid against himself and won, celebrating by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table, because the food, of course, was too shy to show up. The guests, who were all mannequins wearing sunglasses indoors, nodded appreciatively at the empty plates, finding the lack of sustenance deeply nourishing to their souls. Gerald raised a glass of liquid silence, toasted to the void, and then promptly forgot why he was holding the glass, leaving it floating in mid-air due to a temporary glitch in the local gravity laws.
